title: A size measurement should not land its number on the element it measured
goal: When you measure something with one click, the number can end up sitting on top of a neighbouring row or on the element itself, because a caliper only knows to stay off its own thin measuring line, not off the thing it was measuring. The number should steer around the element too.
notes: MeasureContent.subjectRects only covers the measuring line for a plain caliper. EditorState.addElementSize and the Size hover preview in CanvasView both already know the element rect and could feed it to MeasureLabelPlanner.plan as an avoid rect (or a real subject). Watch the interaction with the shortened head from clearingHeadOffset: near an edge there may be nowhere clear, so the planner needs a sane last resort rather than a jump.
acceptance: Measuring the size of a settings row on the audit capture leaves the readout clear of that row
Measuring an element with a neighbour directly below it leaves the readout clear of the neighbour
A measurement with open space around it keeps the placement it has today

log.note: Reproduced on the audit capture (Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/Fixtures/settings-pane-2x.png) before touching anything. Two real failures: (1) measuring the width of a settings row puts the 106x40 readout at y 246-286, squarely inside the row below (234-323); (2) for any element flush with the bottom or right of the picture the head flips inward (clearingHeadOffset last resort) and the readout lands ON the element it just measured - a sweep of 3456 element positions found this all along the bottom border.

Adversarial review before building. (a) The notes suggest an avoid rect; the element you just measured deserves the stronger promise, so it goes in as a real subject (never cover what you are describing), not a soft avoid. (b) Steering around the NEIGHBOUR is only possible when there is somewhere to go: a full-bleed settings row has rows touching it above and below and 96 px margins that a 106 px chip does not fit in, so the honest answer there is to stay put rather than jump into the margin half off the picture. Fallback rule: never off the picture > never on the measured element > clear of neighbours and other readouts > cover as few pixels as possible. (c) Nothing new is drawn: no new chrome, no new gesture. (d) Preview and commit must agree, so the neighbour list is computed once in the canvas and handed to both.

First cut of neighbour avoidance was too eager: probing below a switch on the audit capture picks up a band that overlaps the switch by 5 px (a detection artefact, not a real neighbour), and the width readout slid 93 px sideways to dodge something invisible. Tightened the rule: a neighbour has to actually start on the side it was probed from, so boxes that overlap the element are dropped rather than steered around.

Shipped. Core: MeasureLabelPlanner.plan gained a 'describing' list (the element Size mode just measured is treated as a subject, never covered) and an off-the-picture cost that now outranks covering the subject, so the last resort is the readable one. Core: ElementBounds.neighbors probes the four sides at two distances (touching, and as far out as the number itself travels) and drops containers and boxes that overlap the element. App: the canvas reads neighbours once per pick (memoized) and hands the same list to the hover preview and the commit, so nothing shifts on click. Verified: 1045 tests green, a 3456-position sweep of the audit capture finds zero readouts on their own element (it found them before), and rendered before/after proofs are in queue/audits.
